evidence: src/infrastructure/app.ts: `export function createApp(): Express` is the only place where the repositories (InMemoryUserRepository, InMemoryProjectRepository, InMemoryTaskRepository), use cases, controllers and errorMiddleware are put together.
src/infrastructure/server.ts: only `const port = Number(process.env["PORT"] ?? 3000)` and `createApp().listen(port, ...)`, so it relies on the createApp abstraction without rebuilding the wiring.

Wiring is consistent across resources: UserController(new CreateUserUseCase(users)), ProjectController(new CreateProjectUseCase(projects)), and TaskController with four use cases, each built from repository instances.
No rule or invariant appears in both files; the port setting lives only in server.ts and the middleware order only in app.ts.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files deal with one thing: composing the application and starting it up. app.ts is the composition root. It builds the in-memory repositories, wires them into the use cases and controllers, and puts together the Express app. server.ts only reads the port and calls createApp().listen. Nothing is duplicated between them: the wiring lives only in createApp, and the port and startup code lives only in server.ts. server.ts goes through the module's own createApp abstraction instead of rebuilding the app itself, so nothing bypasses it. Controllers receive use cases, use cases receive repositories, and that pattern holds for every resource. The imports from the application layer are out of scope.
